questions.question: How sharp is the main subject?

real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to fabric-heavy and household scenes (cribs, canopy beds, gowns, quilts, kimonos) when the main subject is clearly lit and in sharp focus. It is weakest on dark or underexposed subjects and on blurry ones. It also responds somewhat less to cool blue or green tinted photos, but the similar units share that. Mid-to-large subjects that fill a moderate part of the frame drive it more than small ones.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to clearly visible, well-lit, sharp fabric and furniture subjects such as cribs, canopy beds, gowns and quilts. It is suppressed when the subject is dark, blurry or very small in the frame. Its strongest particular effects are lighting (medium or bright over dark) and sharpness (sharp over slightly blurry), and it prefers a subject filling a moderate part of the frame. It also leans toward warm rather than cool tints, but similar units share that preference.

real_s3.explanation: Within its fabric, bedding and furniture classes (cribs, four-posters, gowns, kimonos, quilts), this unit is most active on clearly lit, sharp, well-framed subjects. It is strongly suppressed when the main subject is dark, and somewhat suppressed when the subject is blurry, very small in the frame, or under a cool blue or green tint. It also leans weakly toward subjects placed in the right third or facing left. The lighting and sharpness effects are the ones particular to this unit, since its similar units are not unusual on those rows. The cool-tint effect is largely shared with similar units.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to a single, clearly defined main subject (fabric, bedding or garments) that is well and brightly lit, sharp, and placed off-center toward the right of the frame. It is weakest on dark photos and on cluttered scenes with no single main subject. The right-third preference and the bright-versus-no-subject contrast are its most distinctive traits. The similar units are mostly not unusual on these rows, so these traits are particular to this unit.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds to a single, well-lit, sharply rendered main subject such as a fabric item (gown, crib, bed, quilt) or a piece of furniture. It is most active when the subject sits off-center toward the right third, fills a moderate part of the frame, and is level. It is weakest for dark photos, cluttered scenes with no single main subject, and tilted shots. The right-third position effect and the bright-versus-no-subject effect are the most distinctive. The similar units only partly share the brightness effects.

null_s3.explanation: The unit responds to fabric and furniture objects such as cribs, canopy beds, gowns and quilts. Within these classes it is most active when there is a clear, sharp, brightly lit main subject placed off-center toward the right third of the frame. It is weaker for dark subjects, for scenes with no single main subject, and for subjects that fill nearly the whole frame. It also prefers level lines over tilted ones.
